validity.recommendation: no structural change; row is real, correctly classified, not a duplicate of P0182/P2003/P2630 -- it's a distinct FERC docket (CP18-548-000, filed 2018-09-14, certificated Dec 2019) from Eastern Shore's mainline (P0182) and the separate 2017 Expansion Project (P2003, FERC Docket PF16-7-000/CP17-28-000, certificated 2017)
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed independent of GEM. This segment is Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company's Del-Mar Energy Pathway Project, FERC Docket No. CP18-548-000 (application filed 2018-09-14; FERC issued a positive Environmental Assessment May 2019 and a certificate order Dec 19, 2019, Eastern Shore Natural Gas Co., 169 FERC P61,228 (2019)). Confirmed independently by (1) FERC's own EA PDF (www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/CP18-548-EA.pdf), (2) Eastern Shore's own project-archive page (esng.com), (3) a 2019 PR Newswire release issued by parent Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (NYSE:CPK), and (4) Chesapeake Utilities' FY2021 SEC Form 10-K (sec.gov), which states the project 'was placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2021' and that 'Construction of the project began in January 2020.' CLASSIFICATION: correct -- FERC's own EA text (line ~3855 of the extracted PDF) states 'Eastern Shore currently operates the only interstate natural gas transmission [system]...', confirming Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission for an operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate line. DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate. Compared against the roster's other Eastern Shore rows: P0182 (732 mi mainline, 1959) is the pre-existing system; P2003 (40 mi, '2017 Expansion Project') is FERC Docket PF16-7-000/CP17-28-000, certificated Oct 2017, a wholly separate proceeding with its own segments (Fair Hill Loop, Jennersville Loop, Daleville Compressor, Seaford-Millsboro Connector) -- see cross_row_leads. P6003's own docket (CP18-548-000) and facility names (Georgetown East M&R Station, Woodside Loop, Hollymount M&R Station, East Sussex Extension, Somerset Extension) are distinct from both. CAVEAT 1 (minor, not flagged as a concern): the sheet's LengthKnown=20.00 mi is close to but not exact -- FERC's EA states the four segments total 'approximately 19.5 miles,' and the 10-K separately describes '6 miles of pipeline looping...13 miles of new mainline extension' (=19 mi). Both are within ~2.5-5% of the sheet value and both sources hedge with 'approximately,' so this is read as rounding, not a material disagreement. CAVEAT 2 (minor): Eastern Shore's own project page states the last facility (Somerset Extension) was placed in service 'September 2021,' while Chesapeake's 10-K describes the whole project as placed into service 'in the fourth quarter of 2021' (Oct-Dec). Both are Chesapeake's own documents and the discrepancy is a quarter/month rounding matter internal to the company's own reporting, not a dispute with an outside source -- GEM's StartYear1=2021 is correct either way. Opened and read to exhaustion: FERC CP18-548-EA.pdf (full text via pdftotext), esng.com project-archive page, esng.com home page, esng.com/project/2017-expansion/ (cross-row), PR Newswire release, Chesapeake Utilities FY2021 10-K (cpk-20211231.htm, searched for every 'Del-Mar'/'Del Mar' occurrence). Not opened: EIA Natural Gas Data landing page (generic, does not name this project) and the FracTracker national map article (checked -- does not mention Del-Mar or Eastern Shore by name, so it cannot serve as a ref for this row); the two harvested Natural Gas Intelligence links (bit.ly-free, naturalgasintel.com) both now 404 and were about the 2017 Expansion project, not this one, based on their headlines ('...Expansion Approval...', '...NatGas Expansion') -- not chased via Wayback since they route to P2003, not P6003.

validity.recommendation: verify SegmentCost against a primary source; the only cost figure independently located ($37 million, a 2019 pre-construction estimate) does not match the sheet's $46,000,000
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=46,000,000 USD (no ref). The only project-specific cost figure I could locate anywhere is Chesapeake Utilities' own 2019 PR Newswire release: 'The projected cost of the project is approximately $37 million' (with 'anticipated annual gross margin...of $5.1 million'). Neither FERC's EA (environmental assessments do not typically state project cost) nor Chesapeake's FY2021 10-K states a single all-in capital cost for Del-Mar specifically (the 10-K instead gives a multi-year adjusted-gross-margin ramp: $0.731M in 2019, $2.462M in 2020, $4.584M in 2021, rising to ~$6.89M by 2023 -- revenue, not capex). $37M is also only a pre-construction ESTIMATE from the certificate-application stage, and the project ran roughly a year behind its original schedule (EA anticipated construction Sept 2019-Sept 2020; actual construction ran Jan 2020-Sept/Q4 2021), which is exactly the kind of delay that inflates realized cost above an early estimate -- so I cannot rule out that $46M is the correct final figure and $37M is simply stale. I searched Chesapeake's SEC filings (10-K text, financing-activities section) for a specific Del-Mar capex total and did not find one restated in later filings. Flagging as a spec concern with $37,000,000 as the only sourced candidate rather than silently accepting the sheet's $46,000,000, which is currently unsourced anywhere I could find. A researcher with access to Chesapeake's rate-case filings (Delaware PSC / Maryland PSC) or a later 10-K capex table could likely resolve this definitively; I did not chase state-PSC rate dockets given time budget.

cross_row_leads.facts: Chesapeake's own May 2019 press release describes Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company as owning/operating 'a 486-mile interstate pipeline that transports natural gas from various points in Pennsylvania to customers in Delaware, Maryland and Pennsylvania.' This is directly testable against P0182's recorded LengthKnown=732 mi -- 486 mi (2019, pre-Del-Mar's ~19-20 mi addition) is meaningfully less than 732 mi. Worth checking whether 732 mi double-counts distribution mileage, an older/superseded figure, or a different scope than the interstate transmission system Chesapeake itself describes.

Eastern Shore's own '2017 Expansion Project' archive page: FERC Docket No. PF16-7-000 (pre-filing) / CP17-28-000 (certificate); certificate issued Oct 4, 2017, Eastern Shore Natural Gas Co., 161 FERC P61,014 (2017); capacity 'up to an aggregate of 61,162 dekatherms' of additional firm transportation (matches GEM's recorded Capacity=61.00 for P2003); segments: 10.8 mi of 24-in looping (south PA/north MD), 4.5 mi of 16-in looping (PA), 0.5 mi of 10-in looping (New Castle County, DE), 17 mi of 10-in connector (southern DE), 6.7 mi of 10-in looping (southern DE), plus a new 3,750 hp compressor at Daleville (Chester County, PA) and metering upgrades at Lancaster County, PA and the TETCo interconnect near Honey Brook, PA; total capital investment '$117 Million'; in-service milestones Dec 2017 (Honey Brook Meter Station), Jun 2018 (Fair Hill Loop), Jul 2018 (Jennersville Loop + Daleville Compressor Station), Dec 2018 (Seaford-Millsboro Connector + Millsboro Pressure Control Station).

summary: P6003 (Eastern Shore Del-Mar Energy Pathway, FERC CP18-548-000) confirmed real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate -- Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Length/Diameter/Location/Operator all corroborated by FERC's EA plus Chesapeake's own 10-K/press materials, with ProposalYear=2018-09 and ConstructionYear=2020-01 newly filled; SegmentCost=$46M is an unsourced spec concern (only located figure is a $37M 2019 estimate) and Pressure/FuelSource stay UNRESOLVED for lack of any source.
